title: are the *_latest twins of the unread vintage families read by any site?

evidence_definition.the_opener_names_the_twin_path_or_a_tail: the opener call carries a literal that is the twin path or ends with the family directory and the basename
evidence_definition.the_opener_names_only_the_basename_which: the opener call carries only the basename, and that basename contains the family's own name -- the family is attributed, the directory is not proven
evidence_definition.unattributed: an opener names a spelling that carries no family token; it is listed on the row and never counted (no such row exists in this population: all 36 twins are family-named)

class_definition.opened_by_a_source_that_writes_neither_t: the only sources that open it also write neither the twin nor a family face
class_definition.opened_only_by_a_smoke_or_runner_leg: every non-producer opener is a smoke_test.py / run_e* leg
class_definition.opened_only_by_a_one_off_round_script: every non-producer opener is a one-off round script (leading underscore)
class_definition.opened_only_by_the_script_that_writes_it: every opener is in the set of sources that write a latest.json for this family directory
class_definition.reached_only_through_a_glob_and_no_site_: no opener names it; a glob with a literal segment reaches it
class_definition.never_opened_by_any_site_in_the_corpus: no opener and no bounded glob reaches it
class_definition.the_named_twin_is_not_on_disk: the pointer names a twin that is not on disk: unmeasured, not a negative

method_limits: all 36 twins are family-named (36 distinct basenames, no plain latest.json), so a basename-level read is attributable to a family but never proves the directory; sites that name a spelling with no family token are published and never counted

writers are resolved through three channels and every row publishes which one named it; a row with no_write_site_found is one whose writer this corpus cannot see, and any cross-reader of such a twin is only as trustworthy as that gap is small

opener evidence is one AST hop from the call plus the name-resolution e470 applies (4 rounds); a path composed through an argument or an environment variable is not seen, so 'never opened' means 'no opener in this corpus spells it'
the scan reads files that mention latest.json only, so a reader that builds the path from the family directory alone (never the word latest) is invisible
a glob counts only when it carries at least one literal segment (E273's bare '*')
the population is E472's published rows; a family that appeared since is not scanned
reading a twin is not the same as needing its DATED members -- this face prices the twin only, and E478/E481 own the difference between a twin and its vintages
